_comment: How a bank credit is classified. Patterns are case-insensitive substrings of the transaction remarks; first match wins, income_rails before non_income. A credit matching nothing falls through to 'personal' and is EXCLUDED from income. Add a new rail here when a new affiliate network starts paying the bank directly.
_non_income_comment: Real money, but not earnings. Kept separate from 'personal' so the future personal-dashboard can chart owner->mother transfers without re-deriving them, and so they can never be mistaken for income.

_alias_comment: Payer names as the tool you actually recognise. Two jobs: turn a legal entity into a real name, and MERGE a tool that pays from more than one profile so its revenue is not split across two rows. Keys are matched case-insensitively against the payer name from PayPal or the network. Anything not listed falls back to automatic suffix stripping (Inc., LLC, Corp, GmbH, Limited, ООД), which already handles most names — only add an entry when that is not enough.
_alias_evidence: IDENTIFY A PAYER FROM ITS OWN TRANSACTION, NOT FROM A GUESS. PayPal carries the payer email and a free-text note, and the note usually names the brand outright. Pull it with: paypal-txns-pp-cli reporting search-get --start-date <iso> --end-date <iso> --fields all --json, then read payer_info.email_address and transaction_info.transaction_note. On 2026-08-30 a guess (Todor Karlikov's LinkedIn says Book Bolt) merged two unrelated payers; the emails disproved it in one command.

_manual_comment: THE EXIT ROUTE FOR UNTRACED MONEY. When the owner works out where a credit came from - a bank asking about the reference, a payout spotted in a network dashboard - record it here once and it is named forever. This runs before every heuristic pass and outranks all of them (confidence 'confirmed'), so nothing can un-name it. Match is on date + amount, which is unique in a passbook. Copy the date and amount straight off the Untraced row in the dashboard. 'route' is the hops before the bank; 'note' is for your future self, and is not shown in the UI.
